methodB_objectInspection.tool: pypdf 6.19.0, direct page /Resources and content-stream inspection
methodB_objectInspection.interpretation: [INTERPRETATION] Every sampled page's visible content is drawn entirely via vector path-drawing operators (moveto/curveto/lineto, filled), with ZERO font resources, ZERO XObject (image) resources, ZERO text-showing operators, and ZERO inline images anywhere. This indicates the source represents all visible content -- including what looks like text -- as vector-outlined shapes, NOT as an embedded raster/scanned image and NOT as standard PDF text objects with font references. This is a materially different mechanism from a photographically-scanned document, even though the observable symptom (pdftotext returns nothing) is identical.
methodB_objectInspection.hiddenOcrTextLayer: not found -- zero BT (text object begin) operators exist anywhere in the sampled content streams, which rules out any invisible/hidden OCR text layer (which would necessarily use a text-rendering-mode-3 Tj/TJ inside a BT/ET block)

methodC_visualRender.result: All rendered pages show crisp, legible Japanese ledger text and table gridlines with no scan noise, skew, or photographic artifacts -- consistent with vector-drawn content (methodB), not a photographic scan.
methodC_visualRender.imageResolutionEstimate: not_applicable -- no embedded raster image exists to estimate a resolution for (methodB confirms zero XObject/image resources)
